# gd fork: with cgo off, a package that imports "C" whose C cmd/cc can
# build is loaded as if cgo were on, and built with cmd/cc (doc/gd/cc.md).

env CGO_ENABLED=0
go list -f '{{range .GoFiles}}{{.}} {{end}}'
stdout '^cgotag.go $'
go list -f '{{range .Imports}}{{.}} {{end}}'
stdout '^C fmt $'
go run .
stdout '^5$'

# With a #cgo directive, it is not: cgo's files are left out.
cp p.go.ldflags p.go
go list -f '{{range .GoFiles}}{{.}} {{end}}'
stdout '^nocgo.go $'
go run .
stderr '^no cgo$'

# Nor if it uses a C name that cmd/cc does not define, from headers it
# provides (internal/testpty's posix_openpt).
cp p.go.undefined p.go
go list -f '{{range .GoFiles}}{{.}} {{end}}'
stdout '^nocgo.go $'
go run .
stderr '^no cgo$'

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.27
-- p.go --
package main

// #include "add.h"
import "C"

func main() { show(int(C.add(2, 3))) }
-- p.go.ldflags --
package main

// #cgo LDFLAGS: -lm
// #include "add.h"
import "C"

func main() { show(int(C.add(2, 3))) }
-- p.go.undefined --
package main

// #include <stdlib.h>
// #include "add.h"
import "C"

func main() { show(int(C.add(2, int(C.posix_openpt(0))))) }
-- cgotag.go --
//go:build cgo

package main

import "fmt"

func show(n int) { fmt.Println(n) }
-- nocgo.go --
//go:build !cgo

package main

func main() { println("no cgo") }
-- add.h --
int add(int a, int b);
-- add.c --
#include "add.h"
int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
